title: Acceptance and rising
hook: bhaana and chardi kala held together
tomorrow: Bebe asks Arjan's family's last name. why would that matter?

segments.voice: Yesterday, wait with the name: a bead, a breath, Waheguru, while the hot wind blows. Friday came. So did the email.

Half a win can feel worse than a loss. The junior from the bus stop gets a detention and has to apologize to Arjan in person. Good. But the thing Simran actually asked for, a lunch-hour turban day where anyone at school could learn to tie one, gets a polite no. Not this year, too close to finals, maybe next spring. She reads it in the parking lot and texts the family chat a single word: cool. Everyone who knows her knows that cool means the opposite. Bebe replies with one word too: bhaana. Simran stares at it. Is that wisdom, or is it giving up?
screen: `HALF A WIN.` → `A DETENTION AND AN APOLOGY.` → `TURBAN DAY: NOT THIS YEAR.` → `BEBE: BHAANA.`

segments.voice: Bhaana means the Will: what has happened, inside the order of the One. The Japji says, in its second pauri on Ang 1, in paraphrase: everyone is within the hukam, the order; no one stands outside it. So the no from the school is real. It happened. Pretending it didn't, or burning energy raging at it, doesn't change it. Guru Arjan goes further on Ang 394. In paraphrase: what you do seems sweet to me. That's a high bar. But accepting what happened is not the same as approving of it, and it is never the same as quitting. The other half is chardi kala, rising spirits, the spirit that keeps climbing. And the two are held in one breath at the end of the Ardas, the prayer that closes Sikh gatherings: with the Name, rising spirits; in your Will, the good of all. Sarbat da bhala. Here's the part to tell a friend tonight: that closing line doesn't ask for good things for Sikhs only. It asks for the good of all. So: accept the no. Then rise. Simran doesn't get her school-wide day. She does have a lunch table, Arjan, Maya, and a bag of practice cloth in her dad's truck.
screen: `BHAANA: WHAT HAPPENED, IN THE WILL.` · `NO ONE STANDS OUTSIDE THE HUKAM.` · `ACCEPTING IS NOT QUITTING.` · `CHARDI KALA: THE GOOD OF ALL.` · then, large: `ACCEPT, THEN RISE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing that didn't go your way this week. Say quietly what part of it you can't change, and let that part be. Then name one small next step that's still yours, and when you'll take it.
Acceptance and rising. Bhaana and chardi kala, held together: accept what happened, then rise to the next thing that's yours to do.
Keep this one: accept, then rise, in that order, like the end of the Ardas. One lunch table, a bag of cloth, and day 1727.

screen: `DAY 1727 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 101 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: BEBE ASKS ARJAN'S LAST NAME. WHY WOULD THAT MATTER?`

howItsDone: Sikhs close the Ardas, said at the end of gatherings and in daily prayer, by asking for rising spirits with the Name and the good of all within the Will.

fork.setup: you tried out for varsity and got put on JV instead. going by today, what does 'accept, then rise' look like?
options: take the JV spot fully, and ask the coach what to work on next.
quit the team, since it clearly wasn't meant to be this season.
say yes to JV, but keep arguing the decision until it changes.
fork.reveal: bhaana: the decision happened, so accept it. chardi kala: rise to the next step that's yours. accepting isn't approving, and it's never quitting.

original.note: Gurmukhi: bhaana, the Will, what happens within the order of the One.

trapdoor: what you thought: accepting God's will means giving up and staying quiet.
what it means: accept what happened, then rise to the next step: bhaana and chardi kala together.
what a scholar hears: the hukam in the Japji's second pauri (Ang 1); Guru Arjan's 'tera kia meetha laagai' (Ang 394); the Ardas's closing, 'Nanak naam chardi kala, tere bhaane sarbat da bhala'.
guess: taking what happened as the Will, then rising to what's next
giving up on a goal because God has already decided it
staying cheerful by not thinking about what went wrong
recall: without fear, not without feeling it

chat.says: turban day = denied. bebe just texts 'bhaana.' doesn't that just mean give up??
options: no. accept the no, then rise: chardi kala. start it at your table.
yes. if it was in the Will, trying again would go against it.
sort of. bhaana means wait quietly until next spring, then ask.
chat.meaning: Bhaana and chardi kala are held together, even in one line of the Ardas. Accepting what happened isn't quitting: it's where rising starts.

bhaana.meaning: the Will: what happens within the order of the One

hukam.meaning: the divine order everything moves within

chardi kala.meaning: rising spirits, the spirit that keeps climbing

Ardas.meaning: the Sikh prayer said standing, closing gatherings

Sarbat da bhala.meaning: the good of all, asked for at the Ardas's close
